title: Lust Stories 3 Premieres September 18 on Netflix With Motwane, Kiran Rao and Vishal Bhardwaj
excerpt: The International Emmy-nominated anthology returns for an unprecedented third season, featuring Radhika Apte, Ali Fazal, Aditi Rao Hydari and a fresh ensemble across four short films.
body:
• Lust Stories 3 will premiere on Netflix India on September 18, 2026, with four new short films exploring love, desire and intimacy.
  • The third season is directed by Vikramaditya Motwane, Kiran Rao, Shakun Batra and Vishal Bhardwaj, with a cast including Radhika Apte, Ali Fazal, Aditi Rao Hydari and Konkona Sen Sharma.
  • This marks the first Indian anthology series to reach three seasons on Netflix, produced by Ronnie Screwvala and Ashi Dua.
  • Real-life couple Siddharth and Aditi Rao Hydari headline Vishal Bhardwaj's segment, while newcomer Sana Thampi joins the ensemble.

Netflix India's International Emmy-nominated anthology series Lust Stories is returning for a third season, with a premiere date locked for September 18, according to a Bollywood Hungama exclusive. The new installment brings four fresh short films that explore love, lust, relationships and repressed desire through four distinct directorial voices.

A New Directorial Lineup

The third season hands the reins to four of Indian cinema's most respected filmmakers. Vikramaditya Motwane, known for Lootera and Sacred Games, directs a segment starring Radhika Apte, Konkona Sen Sharma, Vijay Varma and Abhishek Banerjee. Shakun Batra, the filmmaker behind Kapoor & Sons and Gehraiyaan, teams up with Ali Fazal and Radhika Madan for his entry.

Vishal Bhardwaj, whose Shakespeare adaptations — Haider, Omkara, Maqbool — remain benchmarks of Indian auteur cinema, directs real-life couple Siddharth and Aditi Rao Hydari. Kiran Rao, fresh off the critical and commercial success of Laapataa Ladies, introduces newcomer Sana Thampi alongside Gurfateh Pirzada in her segment.

"Each film approaches human connection from a distinct point of view, reflecting how desire and relationships are shaped by context, silence and vulnerability."

— The makers of Lust Stories 3

Breaking New Ground for Indian Anthologies

Lust Stories 3 marks a milestone for Indian streaming content. It becomes the first Indian anthology to reach three seasons on Netflix, a format more commonly associated with Western programming. The original Lust Stories in 2018, directed by Anurag Kashyap, Zoya Akhtar, Karan Johar and Dibakar Banerjee, earned an International Emmy nomination and established the franchise as a cultural talking point. The second season followed in 2023 with shorts helmed by Konkona Sen Sharma, R. Balki, Sujoy Ghosh and Amit Ravindernath Sharma.

Each installment has brought entirely new directors and largely new casts, keeping the format fresh while maintaining its core identity — character-driven stories that examine marriages, extramarital connections, class divides and generational gaps through moments of emotional conflict rather than shock value.

What the Diaspora Should Know

For Indian audiences overseas, the Lust Stories franchise has served as a window into evolving conversations around intimacy and desire in contemporary India. The series has consistently challenged conservative norms while remaining accessible to a global audience on Netflix. With filmmakers like Kiran Rao, whose Laapataa Ladies became a sleeper hit internationally, the third season is likely to resonate well beyond India.

The franchise is produced by Ronnie Screwvala's RSVP Movies and Ashi Dua's Flying Unicorn Entertainment. The trailer is expected in the first week of September, according to Bollywood Hungama, with the full premiere on September 18.

Looking Ahead

The writing team behind Lust Stories 3 includes Kiran Rao, Tanaji Dasgupta, Avinash Sampath, Sumukhi Suresh, Shakun Batra, Sameeha Sabnis, Ashwathi Namboodiri, Nitesh Bhatia, Utkarshini Vashishtha and Vishal Bhardwaj, according to Hollywood Reporter India. With filming already completed and post-production wrapped, the September 18 premiere date appears firm. Netflix's slate announcement confirms the platform's continued bet on bold, conversation-starting Indian content.
